purpose: The condition node's comparison semantics, written once and asserted by BOTH
implementations: Loco.Core's ConditionEvaluator (which the engine runs) and the
They are separate implementations in separate languages and they drifted. Before
this table, `"abc" greater_than "100"` failed the node in the engine and
returned false in the simulator - so the tester reported a green run for a
workflow that would die in production. Six of seven probed cases agreed, which
is exactly how a divergence survives: it looks like agreement.
Every case here runs on both sides. A change to either implementation that is
not a change to the other fails one of the two suites.
rules: NUMERIC: a value is numeric iff it is a JSON number, or a string that (after
trimming) matches ^[+-]?(digits[.digits] | .digits)([eE][+-]digits)? and parses
to a finite number. Deliberately NOT the host language's default parse: JS
Number('') is 0 and Number('0x10') is 16, while .NET's TryParse with
AllowThousands accepts '1,000'. Each host would then disagree with the other.
TEXT: null stays null; booleans render lowercase ('true'/'false') so C#'s 'True'
does not disagree with JS's 'true'; numbers render in invariant round-trip form.
equals / not_equals: numeric on both sides -> compare as numbers; otherwise
compare the TEXT forms ordinally. This is the fix: the engine used .NET object
equality, so a {{amount}} resolving to the number 150 never equalled the '150'
typed into the panel, and not_equals confidently returned true.
greater_than / less_than: both sides must be NUMERIC, otherwise the node fails
with a message naming the node, the operation and both values. The engine already
failed here - with a raw .NET FormatException reading 'The input string abc was
not in a correct format', naming neither the node nor the operation - so this
keeps the contract and fixes the message. Ordering non-numbers silently would be
a guess that looks like it works, which is the failure mode this whole branch
exists to remove.
contains: TEXT containment, null treated as empty.
An operation outside the supported list is false, never an error, matching the
engine's `_ => false` switch arm.
